extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychoanalysis, psychologists, literary critics, and researchers of humor/wit
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting psychoanalytic criteria and techniques that define, produce, and explain wit, humor, and the comic (Freud's account). Emphasis on formal linguistic techniques, psychogenic mechanisms, social motives, and classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as a playful judgment / free play of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is a 'playful judgment' or 'free play of ideas' — an aesthetic, non-instrumental mode of thought in which ideas are combined freely for pleasure rather than for serious ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited from Lipps and Jean Paul: 'Freedom begets wit and wit begets freedom.' Usefulness: regard wit as a cognitive attitude (playful contemplation) rather than merely a type of content. Example contexts: witty judgments, aesthetic attitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity (essential quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevity alone is the body and soul of wit; wit 'says what it does say, not always in few, but always in too few words' and often 'expresses itself by leaving the thing unsaid.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for compressed expression and omitting explanatory material that would remove the joke; anti-pattern: long-winded paraphrase which kills the wit (Polonius quote and Lipps commentary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery or unearthing of the hidden / union of dissimilarities
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit often 'unearths something hidden and concealed' and consists in finding similarities in dissimilarities or uniting ideas that are normally foreign to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques that reveal a concealed relation (analogy, surprising association) are productive of wit; classic formula: ability to discover hidden similarities (Jean Paul).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast / antithesis / 'sense in nonsense'
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit frequently exploits contrast or antithesis — the attribution of sense where it is later retracted (sense in nonsense) — producing immediate comic effect by the shift from apparent meaning to nullity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism illustrated by Lipps/Heymans: attribute a meaning to an expression, then recognize it as inappropriate, causing comic sensation (Heine 'famillionaire' example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form/wording over content (verbal/form technique)
rubrics_metrics.description: The witty character often adheres to the mode of expression or wording (form-technique) rather than to the pure thought; paraphrasing the thought accurately typically destroys the wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate wittiness by inspecting the linguistic vehicle (pun, fusion, sound), not only the propositional content. Example: Lipps's paraphrase of Heine's line loses the laugh despite preserving sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation with substitutive formation (blend/portmanteau words)
rubrics_metrics.description: A common technique is condensation that fuses two words (substitutive formation) into a mixed/neologistic word (e.g., 'famillionaire', 'anecdotage', 'kleptorumania').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production guidance: compress two sentences or ideas and fuse salient morphemes to preserve enough cues for the omitted thought; anti-pattern: fusion that obscures reconstruction and fails to evoke the omitted content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation with slight modification / substitution (minimal formal tweak)
rubrics_metrics.description: Witticisms may be produced by tiny formal modifications (a changed letter or syllable) that stand in for omitted harsh content (e.g., modifying 'tete-a-tete' to hint at 'bete').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: remove explicit insult and reintroduce it via a minimal orthographic or phonetic change; effectiveness often increases with the subtlety of modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation by omission (ellipsis implying the omitted thought)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit frequently omits a sentence or clause whose content is reconstructible from the remaining expression; the omission itself is part of the wit (leaving something unsaid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To produce wit, strategically omit the explanatory clause while leaving cues that allow the hearer to infer it; anti-pattern: omission that leaves no reconstructible cue, producing confusion instead of amusement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-division, puns, and sound-based play
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques based on word-division, homophony, rhyme, or sound-similarity (puns, 'sound-wit') create pleasure by inviting alternative segmentations or hearings of an expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include word-division jokes and puns; such devices rely on immediate recognizability of sound parallels and rapid reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity / double meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Witticisms exploit ambiguity or double meaning (polysemy) to produce two concurrent or rapidly successive interpretations, yielding comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design phrases that legitimately support two readings simultaneously or in quick succession; ensure both readings are psychologically accessible so the listener experiences the shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement (psychic redirection similar to dream-work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and humor often involve displacement — shifting affect or meaning from one idea to another — a mechanism analogous to dream-work (substituting secondary elements for primary ones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize displacement in jokes that redirect a taboo or painful idea onto a safer target; in production, use displacement to mask aggressive/painful content while preserving emotional charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure mechanism of wit: economy of expenditure in inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Freud's account: the pleasure from wit originates from an economy in the psychic expenditure of inhibition — wit saves expenditure used to suppress impulses and returns it as pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating wit's psychological effect, consider whether the joke achieves a feeling of 'saved' inhibitory energy (e.g., a suppressed insult delivered indirectly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure mechanism of the comic: economy of expenditure in thought
rubrics_metrics.description: The comic's pleasure arises from an economy of expenditure in thought (e.g., quick mental shortcuts, efficient perception of incongruity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess comic instances for the mental 'shortcut' or economy they permit — rapid comparison or reclassification that reduces cognitive expenditure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure mechanism of humor: economy of expenditure in feeling (defensive transformation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor produces pleasure by economizing affective expenditure — it prevents (or discharges) an expected painful emotional reaction and converts that energy into pleasure (humor as a high form of defense).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate humor by whether it successfully averts a painful affect and turns the potential distress into a humorous pleasure; frequently connected to adult mastery of infantile material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of wit: compromise between unconscious and foreconscious
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit is psychically located as a compromise formation between unconscious processes and the foreconscious; its pleasure depends on two simultaneous modes of presentation (one unconscious, one conscious).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect wit to evoke a Janus-like double presentation in the hearer — part of the reception follows unconscious associative routes, part remains surface-conscious; this double-aspect is central to its effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of humor: foreconscious and defensive function
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is localized primarily in the foreconscious and functions as a defense mechanism that allows conscious confrontation with painful ideas by redirecting affect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying a humorous response, check whether it functions to manage feeling (displace or discharge affect) rather than merely producing intellectual incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification by technical means vs. by speech-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit may be classified either according to technical devices (sound-wit, word-play, blended words, caricature, etc.) or according to its use in speech (repartee, characterization, play on words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For analysis or production, choose the classification that matches your aim: technical taxonomy for form-focused study, speech-use taxonomy for pragmatic/social function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendencies and motives of wit (aggression, cynicism, social aims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit has motives/tendencies: hostile/critical wit, obscene or sexual wit, cynical/skeptical wit, harmless wit, 'tendency-wit' serving political or social aims; these are driven by aggressive impulses, self-elevation, ridicule, or social bonding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the underlying motivation when evaluating a witticism (e.g., insult vs. irony vs. benign wordplay). Social acceptability and ethical evaluation depend on these motives (anti-pattern: mistaking hostile wit for harmless wit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as a social process (transmission and status function)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit spreads socially (like news); it has social functions — confers prestige, bonds groups, advertises cleverness, and appears in autobiographies as evidence of social success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing wit for social effect, consider transmissibility (memorable compressed form) and audience; examples: jokes that become widely retold become social currency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession of confusion and clearness
rubrics_metrics.description: A typical comic/witty mechanism is an initial confusion (incomprehensibility) followed by sudden clarification; the resolution from confusion to understanding produces the comic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design witticisms with a brief enigmatic moment that is quickly resolved by reinterpretation (Heine's 'famillionaire' demonstrates confusion followed by clarifying fusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Janus-like double-facedness (two concurrent presentations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit presents the same content in two different modes simultaneously (one automatic/unconscious association, one conscious surface meaning); the pleasure is tied to this duality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluation, look for dual interpretability; in production, craft utterances that will trigger both an immediate surface meaning and a deeper unconscious associative reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor fused with other comic forms and its role in moderating affect
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor often fuses with wit or other comic types to prevent full emotional development of an affect (e.g., fear, disgust), thus converting potential distress into laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize mixed forms (humor + wit) in which the technique both performs a comic operation and functions therapeutically/defensively; producers can use this to make painful subjects approachable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of infantile remnant / childhood sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Infantile experiences supply material and mechanisms (regression, play) that underlie humor and wit; the humorist can access childhood modes to convert painful affect to pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts of humor/wit should consider whether the content or technique invokes infantile scenes, regression, or childhood modes of pleasure; this explains why certain taboo/sexual themes recur in wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-formation categories and technical labels (blend, neologism, portmanteau, anecdotage etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific technical devices are named and exemplified: blend-words (famillionaire), neologisms (anecdotage), portmanteau, caricature-based coinages, rhetorical travesty/parody, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing witty coinages, preserve recognizable morphemic cues to enable reconstruction of the omitted or fused idea; evaluate by whether the coined form triggers the intended secondary meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production technique: compression / abbreviation as a creative force
rubrics_metrics.description: A compressing or abbreviating operation (collapse of two sentences into one compact expression) is a primary source of wit — the compressed form preserves enough of both sources to evoke the omitted clause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical method: take two related sentences (one qualifying the other), compress them and fuse salient elements; ensure the compressed form leaves reconstructible traces of the omitted qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect expression and allusion as witty strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect phrasing, allusion, and insinuation (instead of direct statement) produce wit by allowing the listener to infer the omitted content and by preserving a socially acceptable surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use allusion to hint at taboo or sharp content, relying on the audience's inferential ability; anti-pattern: allusion too obscure for the audience to reconstruct, losing both wit and communicative effect.
